subject: RFP follow-up: commercial model and token economics clarifications
thread_body:
From: Alice Turner <alice.turner@novabank.com>
To: sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@novabank.com, c.mendez@novabank.com
Date: 2026-10-11 09:12 -0700
Subject: RFP: Commercial/pricing follow-ups — token economics

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the RFP response. Procurement had a few clarifying questions specifically for the commercial/pricing section that we hope you can expand on for our internal evaluation:

- You describe a committed-volume model plus overage. Can you provide an explicit example of how monthly commits, surge usage, and annual true-up would be invoiced?
- Is there a pre-purchased surge buffer option (pre-bought credits) vs. pay-as-you-go overage? If both, can you share unit economics for each?
- Please provide per-token rates for: (a) standard text generation (per output token), (b) chat messages with context (per prompt+response token split), and (c) embeddings (per 1k tokens / per vector).
- Any discounts for quantized model variants or dedicated capacity? How do volume tiers work over a 12-month horizon?
- For Private deployment, please include the commercial overlay: license, per-GPU runtime, and support add-ons.

We also need any sample invoices or line-item CSVs you can share for our SOW and procurement packet.

Appreciate a response by EOD Monday if possible — procurement is on a tight timeline.

Best,
Alice Turner
Procurement Manager, NovaBank

---

From: sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai
To: Alice Turner <alice.turner@novabank.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-11 11:03 -0700
Subject: RE: RFP: Commercial/pricing follow-ups — token economics

Alice —

Thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise commercial example and then the detailed rate cards attached (RFP_NovaBank_pricing_v1.pdf and token_pricing_sheet.csv). I’ll follow up tomorrow with a short internal note on negotiation flexibility.

1) Core commercial construct (dual-layer commit model)
- Baseline Monthly Commit: customer commits to an average monthly token volume (M) for year 1. Committed tokens are invoiced monthly at the agreed committed unit rate.
- Surge Buffer: an optional pool of 'surge credits' can be pre-purchased at a preferential rate (smaller discount vs commit) to cover anticipated spikes. If not pre-purchased, overage is billed at the standard overage rate (higher than surge-credit rate).
- Annual True-up: at the end of the 12‑month term we reconcile committed tokens vs actual consumption. Excess usage is either credited (if pre-purchased surge credits remain) or invoiced as overage according to the overage schedule.

2) Sample invoice (numbers illustrative):
- Committed monthly volume (M): 500M tokens/month
- Committed unit rate (generation tokens): $0.00075 per token (applies to tokens consumed within committed volume)
- Surge credit pre-purchase (optional): buy 100M surge tokens at $0.00090 per token (expires at term end)
- On-demand overage rate (pay-as-you-go): $0.00120 per token
- Embeddings rate: $0.00030 per 1k-token equivalent (or per vector: $0.0025 / vector for 1536-d)
- Quantized model discount: 10% off committed unit rate for INT8 variants; up to 25% off for specialized quantization + batching profiles (requires model approval)

Example month where consumption = 620M tokens:
- 500M covered by commit at $0.00075 = $375,000
- If 100M surge credits were pre-purchased, they apply next: 100M at $0.00090 = $90,000
- Remaining 20M billed at overage $0.00120 = $24,000
- Month total = $489,000

If surge credits were not purchased: 120M overage * $0.00120 = $144,000; month total = $519,000.

3) Volume tiers and discounts (annualized)
- Tier A (0-6B tokens/year): baseline committed rates apply.
- Tier B (6B-24B/year): additional 6% blended discount on committed unit rate.
- Tier C (24B+/year): 12% blended discount + dedicated capacity preferential pricing.
- Discounts compound with quantization discounts (applied to the post-discount committed rate).

4) Private deployment overlay (optional add-ons)
- Private control plane license: $25k/month (includes base support, audit logs retention 1yr).
- Per-GPU runtime license (NVIDIA A100 equivalent): $8k/month per GPU; includes optimized kernel licensing and priority support.
- Enterprise SLA uplift: +1.5% of monthly commitment for 99.9% availability SLA and faster incident SLAs.

5) Invoicing and true-up cadence
- Monthly invoice for committed charge + any surge credits purchased that month.
- Overage invoiced monthly if pay-as-you-go; annual true-up reconciles any pre-purchased credits and issues credit/invoice as needed.

Attachments: RFP_NovaBank_pricing_v1.pdf (line-item examples), token_pricing_sheet.csv (CSV export of per-model rates + embeddings).

If helpful, we can provide a three-month smoothing example (rolling average) for spike protection and a proposal for a capped overage (see options below).

Regards,
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Account Executive — Enterprise, Redwood Inference
(she/her)

---

From: sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai
To: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-13 09:08 -0700
Subject: FW: RFP: Commercial/pricing follow-ups — internal alignment on surge cushion and invoice cadence

Team — forwarding NovaBank’s follow-ups. Key asks from procurement: explicit cap on month-to-month overage exposure, smoothing/rollover mechanics, and a clear comparison between pre-bought surge credits and pay-as-you-go.

Proposed negotiation levers:
- Year1: Offer a 2% introductory credit on committed spend if signed within 30 days (deal-level credit applied to first quarter invoice).
- Overage cap option: cap monthly overage invoicing at 150% of the committed monthly spend (i.e., bill at overage rate up to 150% of M; anything above converts to negotiated surcharge or triggers dedicated capacity discussion). This protects NovaBank from runaway monthly bills while preserving our overage economics.
- Rollover mechanics: unconsumed pre-purchased surge credits roll forward up to 2 months; expire at term end.

Neha — want legal to confirm whether we can commit to a hard cap phrased as 'billing cap' vs. a discretionary 'alert and pause' language. Aditya — confirm if we can commit to the quantization discount guarantee for customer-owned model variants. Marissa — price approval for the Year1 2% credit?

Sofia

---

From: Carlos Mendez <c.mendez@novabank.com>
To: sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai
Cc: Alice Turner <alice.turner@novabank.com>, procurement@novabank.com
Date: 2026-10-15 10:42 -0700
Subject: RE: RFP: Commercial/pricing follow-ups — token economics

Sofia — thanks, the example is helpful. A couple of follow-ups before we move to procurement PO: 

- The 150% monthly cap is in the right direction. Would Redwood consider a smoothing mechanism that allows 3-month rolling averaging rather than a hard monthly cap? That helps with predictable monthly forecasting.
- For the surge pre-purchase, can we get an option to purchase surge credits mid-term and have them prorated into the annual true-up calculation?
- We need a worked example where embeddings-heavy workloads change cost mix (e.g., 30% of tokens are embeddings). Can you include that?

Also please include a short sample invoice showing committed vs surge vs overage line items — procurement requires line items for the external SOW.

Regards,
Carlos Mendez
Sr. Cloud Procurement, NovaBank

---

From: sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai
To: Carlos Mendez <c.mendez@novabank.com>, Alice Turner <alice.turner@novabank.com>, procurement@novabank.com
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-16 15:34 -0700
Subject: RE: RFP: Commercial/pricing follow-ups — refined commercial proposal and next steps

Carlos / Alice —

Appreciate the feedback. Attached is a refined commercial construct and worked examples (NovaBank_final_pricing_v2.pdf). Highlights below and next steps:

Refined commercial terms (summary):
- Commit bands (blended monthly rates shown in attachment):
  • Band 1: 0 - 6B tokens/year — committed unit $0.00078 (generation)
  • Band 2: 6B - 24B/year — committed unit $0.00073 (generation)
  • Band 3: 24B+/year — committed unit $0.00066 (generation) + dedicated capacity pricing options
- Surge options:
  • Pre-purchased surge credits: prorated mid-term purchases allowed; credits counted against true-up at year-end. Pre-purchase rate is mid-point between committed and overage rates (see sheet).
  • Pay-as-you-go overage: standard overage $0.00110 per token.
- Smoothing and caps:
  • 3-month rolling average smoothing available on request (applies to billing calculations for forecast variance).
  • Optional billing cap: billable overage will be limited to 150% of committed monthly spend unless the 3-month rolling average exceeds that; in that case overage is applied based on the rolling average calculation.
- Embeddings and mixed workloads:
  • Embeddings priced at $0.00028 per 1k-token equivalent by default; for vector-priced models: $0.0022/vector for 1536 dimensional vectors.
  • Worked example attached showing 30% embeddings mix and how blended effective cost shifts (see PDF).
- Private deployment overlay:
  • Private control plane + base support: $25,000/month
  • Per-GPU runtime license: $7,500/month per A100-equivalent GPU (volume discounts apply for >10 GPUs)
  • Optional enhanced retention (audit logs, 3yr): +$8k/month
- Invoicing cadence and true-up:
  • Monthly invoice for committed and any on-demand charges.
  • Mid-term purchase of surge credits allowed and prorated.
  • Annual true-up reconciles committed vs actual usage; any remaining pre-purchased credits are carried forward up to two months or credited at the pre-purchase rate.

Commercial concessions offered for NovaBank (one-time):
- Signing within 30 days: apply 2% credit to first quarter invoices (one-time).
- Ability to cap monthly overage at 150% as described (requires legal sign-off; suggested language in attachment).

Next steps:
1) If these terms look acceptable, I’ll route a non-binding commercial term sheet to you for PO prep and our legal team will provide the standard MSA redlines.
2) Procurement to confirm preferred invoice template; we’ll populate a sample invoice (line-items) and send back within 24 hours.
3) If NovaBank wants dedicated capacity options, we can provide a sizing worksheet and a separate hardware-commit proposal.

Attachments: NovaBank_final_pricing_v2.pdf (includes detailed line-items, blended-rate examples, sample invoice), token_pricing_sheet.csv (updated mid-term proration rules).

Looking forward — we can set a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk procurement through the sample invoice if helpful.

Warmly,
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Account Executive — Enterprise, Redwood Inference
